Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR LOWER EXTREMITY FULL LENGTH 
BRACE WITH JOINTS WITH LOCKS 



1. Scope — Requirements of lower extremrty full length brace with joints with locks. 

2. Material 

2.1 Ankle Joint — Coniorming to 18:5809-1970 'Specification for ankle joint with lock for steel 
orthopaedic braces '. ^ 

2.2 Knee Joint ~ Conforming to IS : 5810-1970 ' Specification for knee joint with lock for steel ortho- 
paedic calipers and braces'. 

2.3 Hip Jo/n/ — Conforming to 18:5811-1970 'Specification for hip joint with lock for steel ortho- 
paedic calipers and braces '. 

2.4 Supporting Bands — Conforming to: (a) ' Indian Standard specification for pelvic band ', (b) ' Indian 
Standard specification for calf band', (c) ' Indian Standard specification for thigh band ', and (d) ' Indian 
Standard specification for tuber band* ' 

2.5 Covering for Bands — Thin felt, suede leather and a suitable quality of orthopaedic lining leather 
conforming to IS : 3982-1 966 ' Specification for sheepskin leather for orthopaedic linings '. 

2-6 Rivets and Screws— Mild steel. 

2.7 Loops — Mild steel. 

3. ShapjB and Dimensions — As shown in Fig. 1. 

4. Manufacture, Workmanship and Finish — The two ankle joints and the outer knee joint of the 
brace shall have a loop welded securely to their upper ends. The welding shall be sound and it shall be 
finished smooth by filing to give a neat appearance. The joining of the knee joints to the ankle joints 
at the lower ends shall be by means of two screws each. Similarly the outer knee joint shall also be 
joined with the hip joint by means of two screws. Thei>ands shall be secured by means of rivets after 
they are properly bent to shape. The screws shall have a round head and the rivets shall be neatly fixed 
so as to leave no sharp projections to avoid damage to the clothes of the wearer. The joint components 
shall be bent to proper shapes to suit the contours of the wearer's leg. The ankle, knee and hip joints 
shall be precisely aligned so that their axes coincide exactly with the anatomical axes of the wearer. 
The adjustments for alignment shall be made after assembling the brace temporarily. After adjustments, 
the brace shall be disassembled and the components shall be plated chromium over nickel. The plat- 
ing shall conform to Service Grade No. 3 of IS : 1060-1965 ' Specification for electroplated coatings of 
nickel and chromium on iron and steel ( first revision )'; The brace shall then be assembled again and 
the fittings shall be made permanent. The bands shall then be uniformly wrapped with thin felt and 
covered with suede leather internally then securely covered with externally the orthopaedic lining leather. 
The covered band shall have a neat appearance. The finished brace shall be rigid and well fitting to 
infuse complete confidence in the wearer. Provision shall be made for readjustments or extensions 
later to accommodate the growth of the wearer's limbs. 

5. Marking — Each brace shall be marked with the following: 

a) Manufacturer's name, initials or recognized trade- mark; and 

b) The words ' left leg ' or ' right leg 'depending upon the leg for which the brace has been 
made. 

5,1 ISI Certification l\4arking — Details available from the Indian Standards Institution 

6. Packing — The brace shall be packed as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. However, 
while packing, care shall be taken to suitably protect the brace against getting malaligned in transit. 



Adopted 30 August 1971
